title: Optimize walkthrough - quantization profiles (INT8/FP8) - Lyra Systems
summary: Redwood Optimize walkthrough focused on INT8 vs FP8 quantization profiles, tradeoffs between quality and latency for Lyra's low-latency on-prem inference use case. Discussed benchmarking on Lyra dataset, dedicated vs private deployment, KMS/SSO, and next steps: run quant benchmarks, share perf/quality spreadsheet, schedule pilot kickoff.
transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07; Time: 15:00 PST; Duration: ~60m
Attendees: Sam Carter, Priya Rao, Lena Ortiz (Redwood) - Marta Voss, Oliver Kim, Jenna Park, Ravi Desai (Lyra)
Summary: quick demo of Redwood Optimize quant profiles, walked through INT8 and FP8 results and quality vs latency spreadsheet; agreed to run customer dataset benchmark.

00:00 Sam Carter: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, we have about an hour today, i know lyra is evaluating lower-latency inference options so we wanted to show how Redwood Optimize approaches quantization profiles, especially int8 versus fp8 and the typical quality/latency tradeoffs
00:18 Marta Voss: thanks Sam, yeah we saw your note - our main ask is keep latency under 120ms p95 for short responses and not degrade accuracy on our classification prompts, we also are on-prem k8s with NGC-like GPUs so curious about fp8 support
00:35 Priya Rao: great, quick context - Optimize can recommend quant profiles per-model and per-route; we auto-run microbenchmarks and produce a quality vs latency curve, we also support fallback to higher precision if quality regression is detected
00:50 Oliver Kim: are those fallbacks automatic? like if fp8 drops too much we can route to int8 or fp16?
01:05 Priya Rao: yes, you can set a policy - e.g., prefer int8 for cost, fallback to fp16 for critical routes, and we also have a canary rollout option to test on subset of traffic
01:20 Jenna Park: we operate in a VPC/on-prem model and need KMS integration - does the private deployment preserve key ownership?
01:30 Sam Carter: absolutely, Private keeps control of keys - you can bring your own KMS or HSM, audit logs are local, and we can support SOC2 controls and SSO via SAML/Okta
01:45 Ravi Desai: small nit, do you have proofed docs for FIPS/ISO? we need to present to compliance
01:55 Sam Carter: yes, we'll send the security pack after, includes SOC2 report, network diagrams, and KMS integration notes
02:08 Priya Rao: moving into quant, here's the quick slide - we typically see int8 gives ~1.8-2.5x throughput improvements with minimal quality drop for many open models; fp8 often gives even lower memory and latency but can introduce subtle quality regressions on rare tokens or long-context completions
02:30 Marta Voss: do you have examples on our model class? we run a 7B transformer finetuned for shorter classification and a 13B for summarization
02:45 Priya Rao: yes, our Optimize profiles are model-specific. for 7B int8 usually looks near parity on classification tasks; 13B summarization sometimes loses cohesion in fp8 depending on the quant recipe - that's why we benchmark on your eval set
03:05 Sam Carter: quick demo - i'm going to pull up a quality vs latency spreadsheet we ran internally; note this is synthetic but representative: x-axis latency (ms p95), y-axis quality delta versus fp16 baseline (lower is better)
03:25 Priya Rao: show table: baseline fp16 p95 210ms (13b), int8 p95 120ms, fp8 p95 95ms; quality delta: int8 -0.8% accuracy, fp8 -2.7% on long-form summarization metric, classification delta is nearer 0% for int8 and -0.5% for fp8
03:55 Oliver Kim: okay so for our SLA int8 seems viable, fp8 might be risky for summarization - can quantization be route-specific? like int8 for summarization and fp8 for embeddings?
04:15 Priya Rao: totally, Optimize allows per-route quant profile, you can have the same model served with different quant profiles depending on route or even prefix-based routing
04:32 Marta Voss: how much of that is automated? we don't want to manage dozens of configs
04:40 Priya Rao: we recommend starting with a global profile and Optimize suggests route-level overrides where it sees regressions. also we surface a small set of recommended quant recipes (int8 symmetric, int8 per-channel, fp8 hybrid)
05:05 Jenna Park: how accurate are your auto-evals? we have a handful of labels but not huge sets
05:15 Priya Rao: we accept small eval sets, and we can augment with synthetic probes; still best is your real traffic samples - we run A/B and compute statistical significance for regressions
05:30 Sam Carter: let's talk deployment: Dedicated gives predictable capacity with reserved GPUs; Private deploys inside your VPC with the control plane we operate under a contract. For Lyra's compliance requirements, Private is the usual choice
05:52 Oliver Kim: cost question - how much more expensive is Private/dedicated versus hosted?
06:00 Sam Carter: Dedicated committed capacity is priced differently; we'll send a tailored pricing sheet but typically Dedicated is higher base but lower per-token if volume is large; Private has platform fees for support and on-prem packaging
06:20 Marta Voss: on the technical side, what kernels do you use for fp8? we run NVIDIA A100s and some H100s in prod
06:32 Priya Rao: we pick kernels by hardware and sequence length; for H100 we use the newer fp8 kernels with mixed-precision fallbacks, A100 works well with int8 optimized kernels. Our runtime auto-selects at load-time
06:50 Ravi Desai: who handles model compilation? we want deterministic builds for audits
06:58 Priya Rao: you can compile models in your environment and provide the artifact; Optimize also produces reproducible compilation manifests and we track versioned kernels in the runtime manifest for audits
07:18 Sam Carter: demo - now i'm switching to a short live run: we'll run a quick microbenchmark for 13B summarization on int8 and fp8 using a 5k-token synthetic workload to show p95 differences
07:35 Priya Rao: note - synthetic runs sometimes underestimate tail latency due to caching; real traffic often shows slightly higher p95s
07:48 Sam Carter: int8 run: avg latency 86ms, p95 118ms; fp8 run: avg 63ms, p95 97ms; quality quick-check shows fp8 looses a bit on coherence for the last paragraph in some samples
08:12 Marta Voss: those p95s are promising; our target 120ms p95 looks doable with int8 for 13B and fp8 for 7B perhaps
08:25 Oliver Kim: what's the rollback story if we see production regressions?
08:30 Priya Rao: immediate routing fallback to higher precision variant automatically for traffic that meets the regression detection; plus we support canary + automatic metrics gating so you can avoid full rollouts
08:45 Jenna Park: how does KV cache interact with quant? is there any invalidation nuance?
08:52 Priya Rao: KV cache is independent; quant is at kernel/weights level. cache invalidation works the same - we recommend warming cache on canary to get realistic latency numbers
09:05 Sam Carter: question from Lena: do you do per-token quality tracking?
09:10 Priya Rao: yes we can attach token-level deltas to traces; it's optional but helpful for pinpointing regression patterns
09:20 Marta Voss: if we run your benchmarks on our dataset, how long until we get results?
09:26 Priya Rao: typical turnaround is 5-7 business days for a full Optimize run on customer eval sets, faster (1-2 days) for microbenchmarks; depends on queue and size of dataset
09:40 Oliver Kim: ok, please note our compliance window - we'd like everything for security & perf by Dec 21st for an internal review
09:48 Sam Carter: got it, we'll target that date; we'll need a sample dataset and a short access window to run on your infra if you prefer on-prem benchmarking
10:05 Marta Voss: small follow-up - we use a custom tokenizer and some post-processing steps, will that affect quant results?
10:15 Priya Rao: tokenization won't affect weight quantization but post-processing that affects probability normalization can surface in metrics; we'll incorporate your postproc into evaluation scripts
10:32 Sam Carter: quick pause - any immediate blockers from Lyra folks?
10:36 Oliver Kim: nothing major, just want clarity on rollback and audit artifacts
10:40 Ravi Desai: we'll need the SOC2 and the network topology doc plus an encryption spec; also need to confirm key rotation cadence options
10:48 Sam Carter: we'll attach those docs to the follow-up email and include KMS rotation options and manifest examples
11:02 Priya Rao: another point on quality vs latency: sometimes fp8 can show non-linear quality drops on certain prompts; Optimize flags those prompts and suggests per-prompt routing or hybrid precision (fp8 for most tokens, fp16 for final tokens)
11:20 Marta Voss: hybrid precision sounds interesting - any perf hit?
11:25 Priya Rao: small overhead for switching precision at runtime, but typically the cost is negligible compared to the quality gain; we can quantify in the benchmark
11:40 Sam Carter: moving to next steps summary
11:45 Sam Carter: recap: Redwood will run a full Optimize benchmark on Lyra's eval set, compare int8 vs fp8 vs fp16, produce a quality vs latency report, and propose a rollout plan; Lyra will provide sample dataset, short access window or allow Redwood to run on-prem, and confirm compliance doc recipients
12:05 Marta Voss: agreed, and we'd like a separate sheet that highlights recommended quant profile per route and per model version
12:15 Priya Rao: will include that in the deliverable, with suggested canary percentages and fallback policy templates
12:25 Oliver Kim: timeline again? you said 5-7 business days - aiming for results by Dec 21st?
12:32 Sam Carter: yes, we'll prioritize this and hit Dec 21st if we get dataset before Dec 10th
12:45 Jenna Park: any shared artifacts you'll post?
12:50 Sam Carter: yes, we'll share the spreadsheet, the security pack, and a short demo recording
12:58 Marta Voss: perfect thanks everyone
13:00 Sam Carter: thanks all, we'll follow up with next steps and the ask list
13:08 End of recording
next_steps: Redwood to run Optimize benchmark on Lyra eval set (target results by 2026-12-21)
Lyra to share sample dataset and access details by 2026-12-10
Redwood to send SOC2/security pack and network diagrams
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting after benchmark review
